title: Mutual Fund Tax: How Portfolio Mix Changes Your Capital Gains Bill
description: The capital gains tax on your mutual fund investments depends on the fund's underlying portfolio, not just its category. Funds holding over 65% in Indian equi.

faq.q: How can I check a mutual fund's tax classification?
faq.a: You can check the fund's monthly factsheet, scheme information document (SID), or portfolio disclosure on the AMC's website. Look for the percentage of assets invested in Indian equities. AMFI also provides categorisation details.

faq.q: Does a fund's category name guarantee its tax treatment?
faq.a: No, a fund's SEBI-defined category (e.g., "hybrid," "multi-asset") does not guarantee its tax treatment. The actual portfolio allocation, specifically the percentage of Indian equity holdings, determines its tax classification.

faq.q: What if a fund's equity allocation changes over time?
faq.a: If a fund's equity allocation crosses the 65% threshold (either above or below), its tax classification can change. The tax treatment at the time of redemption will depend on its classification during the period of your holding, which can get complex. It's usually based on the average allocation maintained.

faq.q: Do international equity funds qualify as equity-oriented for tax?
faq.a: No, investments in international equities are generally not considered for the 65% Indian equity threshold. Funds investing primarily in foreign equities are typically treated as non-equity oriented funds for tax purposes.

faq.q: Is the 35% equity threshold for debt funds still relevant after the Finance Act 2023?
faq.a: Yes, for funds with less than 35% equity exposure, all gains are now taxed as short-term capital gains at slab rates, irrespective of holding period. Funds with 35-65% equity exposure are still non-equity oriented with 36-month LTCG and indexation.

faq.q: Where can I find the official tax rules for mutual funds?
faq.a: The official tax rules for capital gains from mutual funds are outlined in the Income Tax Act, 1961, and subsequent notifications from the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT). You can find details on the Income Tax India website.
